$comment: Registry of upstream sources we pull ATS company slugs from. Adding a source is config, not code.
kind:   github-raw (repo + branch + files[].path) | http (files[].url, any host) | file (local path, for manual dumps / CSV exports)
format: json-array (array of strings) | json-objects (+slugKey) | json-keys | text-lines | csv (+column, optional where) | regex-scrape (+pattern, optional between)
Optional per-file: jsonPath ('data.companies') to descend before parsing; where ({column: value}) to select rows of a mixed-ATS table; headers (supports ${ENV_VAR} so API keys stay out of this file).
Slugs are extracted from full board URLs automatically, so pointing `column` at a board_url is usually the most robust choice.
Set enabled:false to park a source without deleting its config.

sources.name: HuggingFace: latmay/ats-career-page-urls
sources.upstreamSchedule: none — a static snapshot (July 2026). Re-check the dataset page for newer revisions.
sources.notes: Not a GitHub repo. Highest-yield single source found anywhere: 7,809 ashby URLs, ~3,855 of them live boards. One CSV of canonical career-page URLs across every ATS; we read canonical_url and let the URL patterns route each row, so one file feeds every ATS. Junk rows (bare integers, $10.2K, .well-known) are dropped by slug validation.

sources.name: One-time non-GitHub backfill (2026-08-11)
sources.upstreamSchedule: n/a — a captured one-time harvest. Common Crawl is the repeatable part; re-run it per new monthly crawl.
sources.notes: Union of four non-GitHub avenues, each slug HEAD-verified live at capture time: Common Crawl index (49 crawls, CC-MAIN-*-index, ~3,300 live), Wayback CDX (jobs.ashbyhq.com domain history, ~3,246 live), a Kaggle ATS company directory (95% live, the cleanest single feed), and urlscan.io + hiring.cafe as new-board tripwires. Ruled out and NOT represented here: Ashby has no sitemap or public directory and its collection endpoints 401; search-engine enumeration is CAPTCHA-blocked; BuiltWith and Wappalyzer do not track Ashby at all; certificate/DNS enumeration is meaningless because every board is a path on one shared host.

sources.name: Workday tenants recovered locally
sources.license: n/a — derived from feashliaa by probing the live API
sources.upstreamSchedule: n/a — regenerated by `npm run repair:workday`, worth re-running if feashliaa ever changes shape.
sources.notes: Not a new source of companies, and in the end barely a source at all: a repair of an existing one that proved the existing one publishes every board twice. 6,055 of feashliaa's 12,884 Workday rows (47%) ship with the datacenter shifted into the tenant field and the tenant dropped — 'wd102|wd1|accenturecareers' where 'accenture|wd102|accenturecareers' was meant. Guessing the tenant from the site name and confirming it against the live API recovered 1,402 of them, of which exactly 5 were boards the store did not already hold: all 6,055 damaged rows duplicate a well-formed row with the same datacenter and site. So the real Workday universe is 6,834 boards rather than 12,884, and the adapter is right to reject the damaged form outright rather than trying to rescue it. Kept enabled because five boards is five boards, and because it is the re-runnable evidence for that claim. Regenerate with `npm run repair:workday`, never by hand.

sources.name: datascry/openroles
sources.license: MIT (code) / CC BY-SA 4.0 (data) — share-alike applies if you redistribute derived slug lists
sources.upstreamSchedule: cron 43 2 * * 1 (weekly-harvest.yml, Mondays) — observed refresh of the tenant lists is roughly biweekly
sources.notes: Largest Ashby list found (4,079) and the only one that ships its own live/dead probe status, which we use to skip boards it already knows are dead. Covers 53 ATS families.

sources.name: kalil0321/ats-scrapers
sources.upstreamSchedule: none — batch commits by the maintainer, roughly monthly (ashby.csv: 2026-07-23 '+592 discovered Ashby boards', 2026-05-23, 2026-05-11)
sources.notes: 3,448 Ashby boards across 46 ATS families, and the only source that ships company display names next to slugs (header: name,slug,url). Actively maintained, just not cron-driven.

sources.name: colophon-group/jobseek
sources.license: AGPL-3.0 (code); see LICENSE-JOB-DATA for the data files
sources.upstreamSchedule: systemd timer 03:00 UTC discovers candidates; additions land as reviewed PRs, ~15-20 companies/day
sources.notes: Freshest source. boards.csv is one mixed-ATS table (5,874 rows across ~40 ATS families) that is the declared source of truth for their production crawler. We read board_url and let the normalizer unwrap the slug, which covers all rows including the ones whose monitor_config uses a non-standard key.

sources.name: Feashliaa/job-board-aggregator
sources.upstreamSchedule: none for slug lists — regenerated manually every 1-2 months (ashby list last touched 2026-06-16). The repo's daily 07:33 UTC cron only refreshes job data and trend snapshots, NOT these company lists.
sources.notes: Biggest single dump of slugs by volume, and the only source here covering bamboohr / icims / paylocity. Flat JSON arrays of strings. Workday entries are pipe-encoded tenant|wdN|site triples.

sources.name: Mayank-glitch-cpu/JobSync-Service
sources.upstreamSchedule: none — abandoned. File lives under legacy/ and last changed 2026-04-14.
sources.notes: Tiny (120 entries) but hand-verified, and contributes a handful of slugs the larger sources miss. Effectively a one-time backfill; kept enabled only because polling it is free.

sources.name: tjwenger/job_scraper
sources.notes: 74 hand-curated slugs scraped out of a Python list literal. Small, but skews toward well-known companies the bulk sources oddly lack (vercel, mercury, snyk, temporal, wiz).

sources.name: crypto-jobs-fyi/crawler
sources.upstreamSchedule: cron 0 8 * * 2,6 (Tue + Sat) refreshes jobs; the company list itself is hand-curated
sources.notes: 365 hand-curated crypto / AI / fintech companies with the ATS named per row. Small, but this vertical is under-represented in the bulk crawls. We read jobs_url and let the URL patterns route each row to the right ATS, so one file feeds every ATS at once.

sources.name: outscal/OpenJobs
sources.upstreamSchedule: none for the company file — harvested and committed by the maintainers
sources.notes: 12,144 companies skewed toward gaming studios and tech, which the general-purpose crawls miss. ats_links is an array of full board URLs per company, so the array is flattened and the URL patterns pick out the rows belonging to each ATS.

sources.name: ConorsCode/open-jobs-data
sources.notes: Only 378 companies, but hand-curated brand names and the one source here with a real daily cron, so it is the fastest to reflect a newly-launched board.

sources.name: Local manual additions
sources.notes: Slugs you add by hand or export from elsewhere (a tech-lookup CSV, a spreadsheet, a probe run). One slug per line; blank lines and #comments ignored. Safe to leave empty.
